title: pylock rejects artifact paths that mix `/` and `\` separators
spec:
This is the `packaging` library (Python 3, no dependencies; the code is in `src/packaging/`). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/property` (about a minute).

```python
from packaging.pylock import Pylock
Pylock.from_dict({"lock-version": "1.0", "created-by": "pip", "packages": [{
    "name": "example", "version": "1.0",
    "sdist": {"path": "dist/files\\example-1.0.tar.gz",
              "hashes": {"sha256": "f" * 64}}}]})
```
Expected: the lock loads and `packages[0].sdist.filename == 'example-1.0.tar.gz'`.
Actual: `PylockValidationError: Name in 'files\\example-1.0.tar.gz' is not consistent with package name 'example' in 'packages[0].sdist'`.

Wheels fail too: a wheel `path` of `"C:/dist\\example-1.0-py3-none-any.whl"` gives `Invalid wheel filename 'dist\\example-1.0-py3-none-any.whl'`. A PEP 751 lock written on Windows can contain paths with both separators in either order (`dist\files/...`, `C:\dist/...`). The artifact's file name is whatever follows the last separator of either kind, and `to_dict()` must still give back the original data.
acceptance: Paths mixing `/` and `\` in either order yield the right sdist and wheel `filename`
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
